d: Install Nostr Vault on an iPhone or iPad, create a Nostr account or bring the one you have, and find your way around.
h: Install · Pick a way in · Create an account · Bring the account you have · Who told you about Nostr Vault? · Find your way around · Next
x: Nostr Vault runs your own Nostr relay on your phone. Your posts, messages and media are kept on the phone, and copies go out to public relays so people can see them. Install Nostr Vault needs iOS 17 or later, on an iPhone or an iPad. Get it from the App Store and open it. The first screen on iPhone Pick a way in The first screen has two buttons. What's inside? above them lists what the app does. Create an account if you're new to Nostr. You get a new key, a password for it and a profile. Bring an account if you have an account from another Nostr app. You bring that account, and your old notes come home to your phone. Create an account Edit Profile. Tap the circle to add a photo, type your name, and tap Next . Both are optional, and you can change them any time. Your key is made for you in the background, and nothing is posted until setup ends. Who told you about Nostr Vault? See below . This key is you. Your secret key is your account: anyone who has it can post as you, and nobody can recover it for you. Tap Show to see it or Copy my key to copy it, then Next . Back up your key. Tap On paper and write your key down, or tap Copy my key and paste it into your password manager within a minute (then the clipboard clears). Don't save it to Photos, Files or iCloud. Tick I backed up my key , then Next . Lock it in. Choose a password of at least 8 characters. Your key is locked on this device behind it, guarded by its secure hardware (Secure Enclave). It never leaves the device and can't be reset by us. If you forget it, your backup is your only way back in. Write it down and keep it with your key backup. Open takes you straight to your feed. Fill your feed. Nostr starts empty: no algorithm picks for you. Tap Let's fill it , pick a few topics, and follow people whose posts you like. Five follows build your web of trust, which fills your feed and filters out spam. Not now skips it. Edit Profile This key is you Lock it in Fill your feed You're done when your Following feed shows posts from the people you followed. Bring the account you have Tap Bring an account . The screen asks Who are you on Nostr? Paste one of these into the box, or tap the QR icon ( Scan a QR code ) to scan one. The app tells you what you'll be able to do: You paste The app shows What you get Your npub, or name@domain Read-only (for name@domain, <name> · read-only ) Your feed, notes and follows. Add your secret key later in Settings to post. Your nsec (secret key) You can post Post, reply, DM and zap. You choose a password, and the key is saved encrypted on this phone. It's never sent anywhere. An ncryptsec (a key locked with a password) Encrypted key · you can post Enter the password you locked it with. A bunker:// link from a signer app Signer link · you can post Your signer app approves each post. Your key never touches Nostr Vault. To use a signer app instead, tap Use a signer app , then Sign in with Clave . See Signers . New to Nostr Vault? Tap Yes, bring my notes from my relays , or, if Nostr Vault is already on another of your devices, Copy from my other vault : On your other device, open Your devices on its Vault dashboard, tap Add and then Show my code (see Link a device ). Here, tap Scan its code and point the camera at it, then let the other device scan this one. If you're asked, check both screens show the same four words, and tap They match . Your vault copies across over the mesh, on Wi-Fi or mobile data, with a moving bar and counts. If the other device can't be reached, the copy keeps trying for a while; then tap Try again , or Continue without it to bring your notes from your relays instead. If the other device has more accounts that can sign, Add your other accounts? lists them. Tick the ones you want and tap Add selected , or Skip . Lost your other device? Tap Lost your other device? We'll bring your notes from relays . A backup .zip is restored later from the Vault tab ( Restore from a backup ). Checking your relays. The app looks for your notes

Android asks you to allow installs from that app the first time. Which file to pick: on the GitHub release, take the APK without "32bit" in its name; it fits most phones. d: Install Nostr Vault on a Mac, set it up from the menu bar, and keep your relay running while the app is open.
h: Install · Pick a way in · Create an account · Bring the account you have · Who told you about Nostr Vault? · Just look around · Find your way around · Next
x: On a Mac, Nostr Vault lives in the menu bar and runs your own Nostr relay. With Start Vault Automatically on, the relay starts when the app opens; otherwise click Start in the menu bar panel. Leave it running and your Mac becomes the always-on home for your notes and media. Install Nostr Vault needs macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later. Get it from the Mac App Store , the same listing as on iPhone and iPad. The first time it opens, a Welcome to Nostr Vault window says Nostr Vault lives in your menu bar . Click Get Started . Setup opens next. The first window after install Pick a way in Create an account if you're new to Nostr. Bring an account to bring your account, your notes and your media. Just look around to read with your public key only. The three ways in on Mac Create an account The same steps as on the iPhone: a photo and name on Edit Profile (both optional), then Next , who told you , see your key on This key is you , write down or copy it on Back up your key and tick I backed up my key , choose a password on Lock it in , then Start Exploring . Your posts go out to our recommended relays; change them in Settings → Relays. The details are on Get started on iPhone . About the password on Lock it in : it locks your key in the vault on this Mac, never leaves it, and can't be reset by us. If you forget it, your backup is your only way back in. Bring the account you have Enter Your Keys. Pick how you sign: Private Key : paste your nsec and choose a password. The key is encrypted on this Mac. Remote Signer : Connect with Clave on your iPhone shows a code to scan with Clave. Or paste a bunker link from any signer app. Your key stays in the signer. No account yet? New to Nostr? Generate Keys makes one here. A key made this way skips the servers step and the profile, so set your relays later in Settings → Relays. Your Vault. Your vault runs on this Mac either way. A Relay Domain (optional) makes it reachable from your other devices. Leave it blank for local only, or tap Skip — configure later . New to Nostr Vault? Yes, bring my notes from my relays goes on to the import. Copy from my other vault links this Mac to your other device with two scans and copies your vault across over the mesh, the same way as on the iPhone . If it can't be reached, your notes come from your relays. A backup .zip is restored later from the Vault tab ( Restore from a backup ). Bring Your Notes Home. Copies your notes from public relays to this Mac, and also reads the write relays you published yourself (it says Also reading from your servers ). Tap Import Notes , or Skip — I'll start fresh . Mirror Your Media. Copies your photos and videos from a media server, or from a backup, to this Mac. Tap Sync Media or Skip Media . Lightning (NWC). Paste a Nostr Wallet Connect link to send zaps, or Skip — set up later . You're All Set. Click Launch Nostr Vault . Enter Your Keys Your Vault Bring Your Notes Home You're All Set Who told you about Nostr Vault? Setup for a new account asks who told you about Nostr Vault, just before the last screen. Paste their profile link or npub, check their profile card and follow them, then pick from the people they talk with most (click someone to see them, then Follow). Skip, nobody told me leaves it out. On a Mac a profile link can't fill this in for you, so paste it. Details on Get started on iPhone . Just look around Enter Your Public Key (your npub or name@domain), answer New to Nostr Vault? , import your notes if you like, and Ready to Browse opens the app. Re-run setup later to post, DM and zap. t: Use Nostr Vault in a browser
d: Open the Nostr Vault web app at nostrvault.app/vault/, create an account or sign in with a browser extension, a signer app code, a bunker link or read-only, and know what the web app keeps in your browser.
h: New to Nostr · Sign in · The first sign-in · Opening a shared post · Find your way around · Browsers · Your data in this browser · Next
x: The web app is Nostr Vault in a browser tab, with nothing to install. Open nostrvault.app/vault/ in any up-to-date browser, on a computer or a phone. Like the apps, it runs your own relay, here inside the browser. Your notes and messages are kept in this browser's storage. New to Nostr The first screen has two choices, Create an account and Bring an account , and Just look around to find anyone by name or npub without signing in. New to Nostr? Click Create an account , then Create My Account . The web app makes your keys in this browser and shows both. Save the secret key somewhere safe, tick I saved my secret key , and choose a password of at least 8 characters, typed twice. Add a name and photo if you like, or Skip for Now . Who showed you this app? finds the person who told you about it, so you can follow them, or Skip . On Fill Your Feed , pick some people to follow. The next screen, Your posts will be shared through these servers , lists the relays your posts go out to: Continue keeps them, Change picks others. Then click Start Exploring . A three-card tour follows, then one question: get notified about replies, mentions and messages while Nostr Vault is open? Turn on or Not now . The secret key stays in this browser, locked with your password; it is never sent anywhere. To see it again, open Settings → Your Secret Key and type your password. Signing out, or the browser clearing this site's data, deletes it from this browser, and nobody can recover it for you. To use the account again, add the copy you saved to a Nostr browser extension, or sign in with it locked with a password (below), or import it in the Nostr Vault app. Sign in Already use Nostr? Click Bring an account . The web app never asks for your plain secret key. Sign in with something that holds the key for you, or with a key locked with a password: A signer app on your phone. Click Sign in with Amber or a signer app and scan the code with Amber, nsec.app or another Nostr Connect signer, then approve. On the phone itself, Open in signer app opens it directly, and Copy link copies the code as a link. This is the way in on a computer with no Nostr extension. A browser extension. Click Sign in with extension and approve in the extension. If this browser has no Nostr extension, the button shows which one to install instead: Sidecar for Chrome, Brave, Edge and Firefox; Nostash on a Mac; and on iPhone and iPad, Safari with Nostr Build Shack or Nostash . Android browsers can't add one yet, so use Amber's code or bunker link. With no extension, the button sits under More ways to sign in . A bunker link. Paste a bunker:// link (or your name@domain) from your signer app into Or paste a bunker link , click Connect bunker , and approve the connection in your signer. See Signers . A password-locked key. Under More ways to sign in , click I have a password-locked key (ncryptsec) , paste your ncryptsec and type its password. The Nostr Vault apps can copy your key this way. Read-only. Type your npub or name@domain and click Sign in read-only , or type a plain name and click Find me to pick yourself from the results. You can read your feed but not post. The sign-in screen in a desktop browser The first time you sign in, the web app asks New to Nostr Vault? Yes, bring my notes from relays fetches them. If Nostr Vault is on another of your devices, No, copy from my other vault links this browser to it with two scans ( Scan your other device , then They match ); the notes still come from your relays, because the web app can't copy over the mesh. Getting your vault ready shows each step; Open now, finish in the background lets you in straight away. Accounts you've used in this browser are listed at the top next time, so one click signs you back in. To keep several accounts signed in, use Settings → Accounts & Keys → Add Account . d: Install Nostr Vault on a Linux machine: the .deb for Debian, Ubuntu and Raspberry Pi OS, the .rpm for Fedora, the Arch package, the Alpine apk, the Flatpak for desktops (arm64 or amd64), Nix and NixOS, the desktop window and tray, and what works today.
h: What you need · Install the .deb (Debian, Ubuntu, Raspberry Pi OS) · Fedora, Arch and Alpine · Flatpak, for desktops (no mesh) · NixOS (flake and module) · On a desktop: the window · Open your vault and link it · Day to day · What works, and what's not there yet
x: Nostr Vault for Linux turns a Linux machine into your always-on vault: a Raspberry Pi, a mini PC, a home server or a desktop. It runs on the machine itself, with no Docker, and starts when the machine does. On a desktop it also has a window and a tray icon, like the Mac app. Your phones and computers reach it on your home network and over the mesh . 3.3.0 is the first stable Linux release. Every package is on the GitHub release v3.3.0 . What works and what doesn't yet is at the end of this page . What you need A 64-bit machine: arm64 (a Raspberry Pi 4 or 5) or amd64 (x86-64). A 32-bit system is refused. One of these systems, each with its own package in the release: Debian 12 or newer, Ubuntu 22.04 or newer, or Raspberry Pi OS 12 (64-bit): the .deb . Fedora : the .rpm (checked with SELinux enforcing). Arch Linux and Arch Linux ARM: the .pkg.tar.zst . Alpine 3.22 or newer: the .apk (OpenRC, no window or tray). Any desktop with Flatpak (Steam Deck, Fedora Silverblue, Bazzite and others): the .flatpak . It has no mesh for now. NixOS : the flake's NixOS module, below . Your npub , the public key of the account that owns the vault. The machine never gets your secret key. Room to store your notes and media. A USB SSD is much better than an SD card; see Raspberry Pi . Install the .deb (Debian, Ubuntu, Raspberry Pi OS) Open a terminal on the machine (or ssh into it) and download the file for your machine from the 3.3.0 release : …_arm64.deb for a Raspberry Pi or other ARM board, …_amd64.deb for a normal PC. Then: sudo apt install ./nostr-vault_3.3.0+7282_arm64.deb sudo nostr-vault-setup --owner npub1… On a machine with no screen, add --no-install-recommends to the first line so apt skips the window's libraries. nostr-vault-setup also takes --data /path for where the vault lives (a USB SSD is much better than an SD card) and --port (8080 to start). It starts the vault and prints the address to open, for example http://192.168.1.20:8080/ . Use the file name you downloaded: the number after 3.3.0+ is the build. Check the file first against SHA256SUMS in the release: sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS . Fedora, Arch and Alpine Download the package for your system and machine from the 3.3.0 release ( x86_64 for a normal PC, aarch64 for ARM), then install it and set the owner: # Fedora sudo dnf install ./nostr-vault-3.3.0+7282-1.x86_64.rpm # Arch Linux sudo pacman -U ./nostr-vault-3.3.0+7282-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst # Alpine (as root) apk add --allow-untrusted ./nostr-vault-3.3.0_p7282-r0.x86_64.apk sudo nostr-vault-setup --owner npub1… # on Alpine, as root: nostr-vault-setup --owner npub1… Each one is the same vault as the .deb , with the mesh, and runs the vault and the mesh as their own users, nvvault and nvmesh . On Fedora the package labels its programs for SELinux, so they run as an ordinary service. The .rpm and Arch package have the window and tray like the .deb (on Arch, pacman -U brings the window's packages with it on Arch); the Alpine apk has none, so open the vault from another device. On Alpine the services are OpenRC's: rc-service nostr-vault stop , and the logs are in /var/log/nostr-vault/ . The Alpine apk is signed with a throwaway key made for this build, so apk needs --allow-untrusted . Check the file against SHA256SUMS in the release first. Flatpak, for desktops (no mesh) Download nostr-vault-…-x86_64.flatpak (or aarch64 ) from the 3.3.0 release , then: flatpak install --user ./nostr-vault-3.3.0+7282-x86_64.flatpak Open Nostr Vault from your apps. The Flatpak is different from the packages above: No mesh. Device sync is off in the Flatpak for now. Your phones reach this vault on your home network only, not away from home. The vault and the tray only , and it runs only while you're logged in . It starts at login (your desktop asks once) and keeps running when you close the window; quit it from the tray or with Ctrl+Q. d: Run your Nostr Vault on a Raspberry Pi 4 or 5 with no screen: 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS, a USB SSD instead of the SD card, the install steps, the address to open and the ports it uses.
h: What to use · Install · Ports and your router · Keeping it healthy
x: A Raspberry Pi on a shelf makes a good always-on vault: it uses little power, stays on, and your phones reach it at home and over the mesh. This page adds the Pi details to Get started on Linux . What to use A Raspberry Pi 4 or 5. The vault is capped at 1.5 GB of memory and the mesh at 512 MB, so a model with more memory leaves room for other things. Raspberry Pi OS 12 (Bookworm), 64-bit. The 32-bit system won't install: the vault needs arm64. Raspberry Pi OS Lite, with no desktop, is fine. A USB SSD for the vault. A vault writes all the time. An SD card wears out and is slow; a USB SSD lasts much longer. Plug it in before you install and give its folder to nostr-vault-setup --data . A wired network if you can. Wi-Fi works too. Install Set up the Pi with Raspberry Pi Imager, turn on SSH, and log in from your computer: ssh you@raspberrypi.local . Download …_arm64.deb from the release and install it as in Get started on Linux , with --no-install-recommends on a Pi with no desktop so it installs only the vault, not the window. Run sudo nostr-vault-setup --owner npub1… --data /media/you/ssd/nostr-vault with your account's npub and a folder on your SSD. When it's done it prints the address. Open http://raspberrypi.local:8080/ (or the IP address it printed) on your phone or computer, sign in, and pair the box with your phone: see A Linux box in My Devices . Ports and your router The vault answers on port 8080 on your network. Pick another with sudo nostr-vault-setup --port … . The engine (3355) and the mesh door (8081) listen only on the Pi itself. Nothing opens a port on your router. Away from home, your own devices reach the Pi over the mesh, and the Pi answers only them. Keeping it healthy The vault starts by itself when the Pi boots. If the Pi loses power, it comes back on its own. Watch it with journalctl -fu nostr-vault -u nostr-vault-mesh , or open the box's page in Settings for memory, disk and mesh status. Running out of room? Plug in a bigger drive and use Move vault to… on the box's page. To update, install the newer .deb the same way. Your data, owner and port stay.

d: Install Nostr Vault on umbrelOS from the Nostr Vault community app store: add the store, install, claim the box with your npub and the setup code, pair your phone, and what a restore means.
h: Add the store and install · Claim the box · Pair your phone · Updates · Backups and restore · Where the data is
x: umbrelOS runs Nostr Vault as an app on your Umbrel: the same box as Nostr Vault for Linux , with umbrelOS doing the installs and updates. It comes from our own community app store, so you add the store once and install from it. Add the store and install On your Umbrel, open App Store , then the ⋯ menu at the top right, then Community App Stores . Paste https://github.com/btcforplebs/umbrel-app-store and tap Add . Open Nostr Vault from the new store and tap Install . It runs on Umbrel Home, Raspberry Pi and other x86 or arm64 Umbrels. Claim the box A new box serves only a setup page until its owner claims it. On the app's page in umbrelOS, look under Default credentials . The password there is the box's setup code . It is also in the app's settings. Open the app. Paste your account's npub (never your nsec: the box never holds your private key) and the setup code, and tap Claim this box . Sign in on the box's page with the same account (a signer extension or a bunker). The first npub with the right code owns the box, and the setup page is gone after that. Only that account can manage the box. Too many wrong codes in a minute and the box waits before it accepts more. Pair your phone Pair from the box's page, as for any Linux box: Settings → This Box → My Devices → Add a device , scan the code with Nostr Vault on your phone, and check that both show the same four words. The steps are in A Linux box in My Devices . At home your phone links to the box over your network. Away from home it reaches the box over the mesh, with no router ports opened. The app uses host networking so the mesh can offer your phone the Umbrel's real network address. Updates umbrelOS offers each new version under Updates in the App Store. The box's own Update button says the same. Your data, owner and paired devices stay. Backups and restore umbrelOS backups copy the whole vault except the box's mesh key (with its old npub and mesh status). After a restore the box makes a new mesh key, so it has a new npub. Your account, notes and media are all there, but your phone still knows the old box: on the phone, remove the old box under My Devices ( Remove a device ) and pair the box again. Where the data is The vault lives in the app's data folder on your Umbrel ( ~/umbrel/app-data/nostrvault-nostr-vault/data ). Uninstalling the app deletes it, so back up first. The box's Move vault to… is turned off here: umbrelOS owns the disk.

d: Install Nostr Vault on a Start9 server running StartOS 0.4: sideload the .s9pk from the release, set the owner npub, trust the server's certificate on your phone, pair your phone, and what a restore means.
h: Install (sideload) · Set the owner · Pair your phone · Updates · Backups and restore · Storage
x: StartOS runs Nostr Vault as a service on your Start9 server: the same box as Nostr Vault for Linux , with StartOS doing the install, backups and HTTPS. Until it is listed in the StartOS Marketplace, you install it from a file on our release. Install (sideload) Download the package for your server from the latest release : nostr-vault-…_x86_64.s9pk for most servers, or nostr-vault-…_aarch64.s9pk for a Raspberry Pi or another ARM server. The …-startos.sha256 file beside them lists their checksums. In StartOS, click Sideload in the top bar and drop the file in. Check the package details and click Install . StartOS warns that no key you trust signed it; confirm to go on. Keep the tab open while it uploads. Set the owner Open Nostr Vault under Services . It won't start until it has an owner: run the Set owner npub action and paste your account's npub (never your nsec: the box never holds your private key). Start the service and wait for both health checks, Web Interface and Mesh . Mesh says "Waiting for a device" until you pair one. Open the Web UI and sign in with the same account (a signer extension or a bunker). The Web UI uses your server's own HTTPS certificate. A phone or computer that opens it by its .local name or LAN address needs your server's root CA installed and trusted, as for any other StartOS service. Start9's guide covers it: docs.start9.com , "Trusting your Root CA". Pair your phone Pair from the box's page, as for any Linux box: Settings → This Box → My Devices → Add a device , scan the code with Nostr Vault on your phone, and check that both show the same four words. The steps are in A Linux box in My Devices . The Show box npub action shows the box's own mesh npub (text and QR code), if you would rather add the box on your phone with Paste instead . Away from home your phone reaches the box over the mesh, with no router ports opened. On your own network the box offers your phone its LAN address on UDP port 47821. Updates To update, sideload the newer .s9pk the same way; StartOS offers Update instead of Install. Your data, owner and paired devices stay. The box's own Update button points you to StartOS. Backups and restore StartOS backups copy the whole vault except the box's mesh key (with its old npub and mesh status). After a restore the box keeps its owner and makes a new mesh key, so it has a new npub. Your notes and media are all there, but your phone still knows the old box: on the phone, remove the old box under My Devices ( Remove a device ) and pair the box again. Storage The vault lives on the StartOS data drive. The box's Move vault to… is turned off here: StartOS owns the disk.

d: What your Nostr keys are, where Nostr Vault keeps them, and how to add accounts, switch between them, back up your secret key and remove a key.
h: Two keys · Where to find them · Watch-only accounts · Add another account · Switch accounts · Back up your secret key · Other secrets the app keeps · Change how an account signs · Remove a key or an account · Leave Nostr Forever · Your relay list · Next
x: A Nostr account is a pair of keys. Nostr Vault keeps them on your device, or leaves the secret one with a signer app, and never on a server. Two keys Public key (starts with npub ): your name on Nostr. Share it freely. With only this, an app can show your feed but can't post as you. Secret key (starts with nsec ): your password to Nostr. Anyone who has it can post as you, forever. Nobody can reset it or recover it for you, not even us. Nostr Vault can sign for you in two ways: A local key. Your secret key, locked with a password you choose (at least 8 characters), and kept on this device only. A key locked this way starts with ncryptsec . This password locks your secret key. It stays on this device only and is never sent to us or any server. We cannot recover or reset it. If you forget it, your saved secret key is your only way back in. A signer. A separate app holds your secret key and approves each post. Nostr Vault never sees the key. See Signers . Where to find them Device Open iPhone, iPad, Android Profile tab → gear → Accounts & Keys Mac Settings at the bottom of the rail → Account → Accounts & Keys Web Settings → Accounts & Keys Each account shows how it signs: Local Key , Remote Signer , Amber (Android), or No signing key (read-only). The first account you set up is the Owner : it's the one your vault belongs to. Tap an account to manage it. On iPhone, iPad and Mac it opens its own page; on Android its row opens in place. Watch-only accounts An account with only its npub can read, but not post, like or send messages. In your vault: iPhone, iPad and Mac give it its own space, so the vault keeps its notes and uploads and shares them like yours. It can't read your private notes or add to them. Android keeps it out of the vault until it has a key or signer on the phone. Add a key or signer and it reads the private side like the owner. Remove the key or signer again and it goes back to watch-only. See Every account on this device . Accounts & Keys on iPhone An account on iPhone An account on Android Add another account In Accounts & Keys , tap Add Account . Paste the account's key. iPhone, iPad and Mac take its npub. Then open the new account and tap Import Private Key or Connect Remote Signer to post with it. Android takes an npub, an nsec or an ncryptsec, or Connect Remote Signer (NIP-46) . Web signs in with the account's own extension or bunker. The account you're using stays signed in. Accounts & Keys on Mac Switch accounts iPhone: hold your picture in the middle of the tab bar and pick an account. It only opens when you have more than one. Mac: click your picture at the top of the rail and pick an account. Everywhere: open the account in Accounts & Keys and tap Switch to This Account . A post is always sent from the account that was active when you tapped Post. Back up your secret key Do this once, right after you make an account, and keep the key in a password manager. Open the account in Accounts & Keys . Tap Reveal Key (Android: Reveal Private Key ). The app checks it's you with Face ID, Touch ID or your device passcode, then asks for the key's password. Copy the key into your password manager. Don't paste it into a chat, a note or a screenshot. Reveal Private Key, still locked With a signer, there's no key to reveal here. Back it up in the signer app. Other secrets the app keeps Your wallet connection and your signer links are secrets too: whoever has them can spend from your wallet or ask your signer to sign. Since 3.2.2 they're no longer in the app's settings file. On iPhone, iPad and Mac they're in the Keychain, on this device only. On Android they're in the phone's encrypted key store. They move there by themselves the first time you open 3.2.2. Change how an account signs Import Private Key adds a local key to an account that only had a public key or a signer. Tick Encrypt with Password to lock it. Connect Remote Signer adds a signer. It must hold this account's key; a signer for another account is refused. Wi

d: Keep your Nostr secret key out of Nostr Vault with a signer: Amber on Android, Clave on iPhone, a bunker link from any signer app, or a browser extension on the web.
h: Which signer, where · Sign in with a signer during setup · Add a signer to an account you already have · On the web · Good to know
x: A signer is a separate app that holds your secret key. When Nostr Vault wants to post, like or send a message as you, it asks the signer, and the signer approves. Your key never enters Nostr Vault, so a problem in Nostr Vault can't leak it. Which signer, where Device Signers How it connects Android Amber, or any signer app on the phone Use Amber , or Use a signer app → Sign in with a signer app iPhone and iPad Clave Use a signer app → Sign in with Clave Mac Clave on your iPhone Connect with Clave on your iPhone shows a code to scan Web A Nostr browser extension. On iPhone and iPad: Nostr Build Shack or Nostash in Safari Sign in with extension Everywhere Any signer that gives a bunker link (NIP-46), such as nsec.app or your own bunker Paste or scan the bunker:// link Sign in with a signer during setup Choose Bring an account . On iPhone and Android, the next screen has Use a signer app under the box (and Use Amber on Android when Amber is installed). On a Mac, choose Remote Signer . The signer opens, or a code shows on screen to scan with a signer on another device. Approve the connection in the signer, then come back to Nostr Vault. If the signer didn't open, tap Open Clave again (Android: Open signer again ), or Copy link and open it yourself. Or paste a bunker:// link from any signer app into the same box. Remote Signer on Mac: Connect with Clave on your iPhone Add a signer to an account you already have Open Settings → Accounts & Keys and tap the account. Tap Connect Remote Signer . Paste the bunker link into Bunker URI , or scan its QR code. On iPhone you can Sign in with Clave here too. Approve the connection in your signer app. Connect a signer on iPhone Connect Remote Signer on Android The signer has to hold this account's key. A signer for a different account is refused. On the web An account you already have signs on the web with a signer: a browser extension, a signer app on your phone ( Sign in with Amber or a signer app shows a code to scan), or a bunker link in Or paste a bunker link and Connect bunker . It never asks for that account's secret key. (An account made with Create an account on the web keeps its key in that browser, locked with your password: see Use Nostr Vault in a browser .) A bunker's connection to the browser is stored encrypted, and removing the account or signing out asks the bunker to drop it. Good to know Posts, likes and messages are signed by the signer, which may ask you to approve each one. If nothing happens, open the signer and check for a pending request. Sending to your own devices doesn't need the signer. Since 3.2.2, with a bunker (or Amber on Android) the posts, photos and files you send reach the devices in Your Devices without a tap: the phone signs those sends with its own mesh key. Only a copy to a public media server still asks your signer. To stop using a signer, open the account and tap Disconnect Remote Signer . Revoke the connection in the signer app too. Back up your secret key in the signer app. Nostr Vault can't show it to you, because it never has it.

d: How the Nostr Vault wallet works: connect a Lightning wallet with a Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) link, turn on zap buttons, disconnect, and the on-chain Bitcoin address under Advanced.
h: What the wallet is · Connect a wallet · Turning on zap buttons · Saving the wallet to your Nostr account · Disconnecting · Bitcoin On-Chain · The Wallet Connect tutorial
x: The basics What the wallet is A zap is a small bitcoin tip sent over Lightning (bitcoin's fast payment network) to the person who posted. Amounts are in sats , the smallest unit of bitcoin. Nostr Vault never holds that money. Your sats stay in a Lightning wallet you run somewhere else, such as Alby Hub, Coinos, Primal or Zeus. Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) is a standard way for an app to ask that wallet to pay. Your wallet gives you a link that starts with nostr+walletconnect:// , and you paste it into Nostr Vault. Treat the link like cash. Anyone who has it can spend from that wallet. If your wallet lets you, make a connection with a spending limit just for Nostr Vault. Step by step Connect a wallet In your wallet app, find Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) and copy the connection link. In Nostr Vault, open Settings → Account → Wallet . Paste the link into the Wallet Connect box (on Android it's called Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC) ). On the web, tap Connect a wallet , paste the link, then tap Connect wallet . The app pastes the link only. There is no QR scanner for it. Once a wallet is connected you'll see its Balance and can set your Default Zap (on Android, Default Zap Amount (sats) ), the amount one tap sends. On the web, Default zap is there even before you connect. On every device, including the web, you can also start from your own profile. Tap the bolt (labelled Lightning in the apps, Wallet on the web). With no wallet yet, it shows No Wallet Connected and a Connect a wallet button that takes you to the same place. On Android the wallet is on the Settings tab of that screen. Once connected, that screen shows your balance and lets you receive with an invoice, pay an invoice, lightning address or LNURL, and see your history if your wallet shares it. Opt in Turning on zap buttons Zap buttons on posts are a choice you make under Settings → Appearance → Post buttons . Add ⚡️ in the Add ⚡️ field to show a zap button, and remove it to hide the button. Zapping someone from their profile is always available. iPhone, iPad and Mac: the zap button is off until you add ⚡️. It then shows on posts, live streams and locked articles. Android: ⚡️ is there by default, so posts show a zap button until you remove it. Web: notes show a zap button. A tap sends your default zap, and holding it lets you pick another amount. Turn off Zap button ⚡️ under Settings → Post buttons to hide it. Tap the bolt to send your default zap, or hold it to pick another amount, on every note row and in threads (iPhone, iPad, Android and the web). On the Mac, right-click a post or a profile's zap button and pick Zap… . A one-tap zap is never less than 1 sat. When the wallet is slow A wallet can take a minute or more to pay. The app waits about 90 seconds for it and watches for the zap's receipt, so a zap that went through no longer shows as failed. Since 3.3.0 it keeps looking for the receipt for up to 10 minutes, and the waiting pill has Pay in wallet app , which opens the same invoice in your wallet app so you can finish there (iPhone, iPad and Mac). If the wallet hasn't answered yet, the pill says Sent, waiting for your wallet (Android: "Sent. Your wallet hasn't confirmed yet, so it may still arrive."). That means it may still pay, not that it failed. When the receipt arrives, the bolt lights and it says Zapped . Zap the same post again while the first is still on its way and the app asks first ( Zap again? on iPhone, iPad and Mac), so you don't pay twice by accident. A real error from your wallet still shows as a failure. Each zap goes straight from your wallet to the author. Nostr Vault takes no cut. Before your wallet pays, the app checks that the invoice asks for exactly the amount you chose, and refuses one that asks for more or names no amount (Android). d: Nostr Vault feeds: Following, Discover, Global, Popular, Media and the rest; Edit Feeds; the Web of Trust shield; languages; reposts, replies and auto-load; and how a new account fills its feed.
h: The feeds · Edit Feeds · Web of Trust or Everyone · Reach: how far a feed goes · The buttons at the top · New posts · Your wider network · Links open in the app · Feed & Display · Spam and blocking · Filling an empty feed · On each device
x: The feeds Tap the feed name at the top left of the Feed tab to switch. On iPhone you can also hold the Feed tab and slide up. Following : people you follow. It's always on. Catch Up : the newest post from each person you follow, one each, from the last two weeks. Quiet people don't get lost under busy ones. Discover : the people your follows follow. It leaves out people you already follow and anyone outside your web. Underrated : good posts from people one step out, never your own follows. Ranked by the likes, reposts and zaps they get from your web, with a lift for people who post less. Global : everyone in your web of trust , without replies. Hashtags : the hashtags you follow. Popular : what's getting the most replies, reposts, likes and zaps. On iPhone, iPad, Mac and the web it shows only your web. Media : photos and videos. diVines : short looping videos. Articles : long-form posts. An edited article shows once. Recipes : recipes posted for zap.cooking. Marketplace : things for sale. Live : live streams, loaded fresh each time. Polls : polls you can vote in. Music : tracks from Wavlake. Pick yours Edit Feeds Open the feed menu and tap Edit Feeds at the bottom. Tap a feed to show or hide it. Drag a feed to move it. On Android, drag the handle. Tap Reset to Default to start over. Following can't be hidden. If you hide the feed you're on, you go back to Following. Spam stays out Web of Trust or Everyone Global, Hashtags, and the Global side of Media, Articles, diVines, Recipes, Live, Marketplace and Polls show only people in your web of trust: people you follow and the people they follow. A shield at the top right says Web of Trust . Tap it to switch to Everyone . You'll get a Sensitive Content Warning first, because Everyone is unfiltered and you should expect spam. It starts on Web of Trust. While Everyone is on, Global shows a banner saying so, with Back to your web to switch back in one tap (iPhone, iPad, Mac and the web). Everyone stays locked until you follow at least 5 people. Until then the shield shows a lock, and tapping it explains why: Everyone is locked , how many of the 5 you follow, and how many more to go, for example "Follow 3 more people to unlock Everyone". Follow a few people and the switch opens. If you had already turned Everyone on, it stays on. If your web isn't built yet, Global and Media stay empty. Hashtags and Live show everyone instead, so you can find your first people. Live still leaves out adult streams. New in 3.2.3 Reach: how far a feed goes On iPhone, iPad, Mac and the web, every feed now goes through the same check against your web of trust. A note from outside your web never lands in a feed, not even one that tags you. Those wait in the Vault under Outside your web . Discover, Global, Popular, Underrated and Media each have a Reach setting under Settings → Feed (on the web: Following, Discover, Global, Hashtags, Popular, Media and Relay feeds): Your web : your follows and the people enough of them follow. This is where most feeds start. Your web + a few one hop out (web: + a few one hop out ): also a few posts from one step further out, at most one per person and never replies. Underrated starts here. Following and Catch Up are your follows, so they have no Reach. Global's Everyone shield still shows everyone, except people you blocked or muted. Under a post, replies and quotes from outside your web fold into one Outside your web line. A switch under Settings → Feed (Show Outside your web under posts, on to start) hides that line; the notes stay in the Vault. Android has the per-account web and the Everyone shield, but not Reach yet. Tune a feed The buttons at the top Each feed shows the buttons that make sense for it. Reposts and Auto-load on Following, Discover and Global, and Replies on Following and Discover. Global never shows replies. These are the same switches as in Settings, so turning one off here turns it off everywhere. Languages on Global: pick one or more, or All languages .

d: Nostr Vault messages and notifications: where Messages is, starting a message, NIP-17 and NIP-04, photos, DM relays, who can message you, the Vault activity list, notification settings and in-app pills.
h: Where your messages are · Start a message · Sending a photo or video · Sending, Not sent, Try again · NIP-17 and NIP-04 · DM relays and who can reach you · Your notifications · Notification settings · No push server
x: Where your messages are iPhone and Android: open the Vault tab and tap the envelope at the top right. A red dot means something is unread. iPad: Messages in the sidebar, with an unread count. Mac: Vault in the rail, then Messages in the bar at the top. Web: Messages on the Vault tab, or in the sidebar on a computer (shortcut g m ). Write to someone Start a message In Messages, tap the compose button ( New Message ). Type a name, or paste a key: an npub, an nprofile, a 64-character hex key or a nostr: link all work, even for someone whose profile hasn't loaded. It says so when nothing matches, the key is bad, or the key is your own. Pick the person. Their conversation opens, with its history, and you write there. People you've blocked never come up, and pasting a blocked person's key says so. A conversation with someone you blocked shows no messages, and its message box is off. You can also tap Message on someone's profile or on their card in the WoT tab, or Message seller on a Marketplace listing, which fills in the listing for you. On the web, type a name or paste an npub and tap Open . Opening a conversation marks it read. Mark all as read is at the top of the list. Read state stays on each device. Photos and videos Sending a photo or video In a conversation, tap the photo button ( Attach photo or video ; web: Photo), paste a photo with Paste Photo , or drag it in on a Mac or iPad. On iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android the same button sends videos too, and so does the web app. Photos other than GIFs are re-saved, which removes their location, and a GIF's hidden extras (comments and other metadata) are stripped. With Upload Quality set to Original, a photo goes at full size instead, with only its location removed. Since 3.2.3 a photo or video in a NIP-17 message is locked : the app encrypts it on your device before it uploads, so the media server only ever holds scrambled bytes, and the key travels inside the sealed message. It goes to your own media servers, or to nostr.download if they refuse it. Videos are capped at 100 MB (Android shrinks a big clip first). A received PDF or other file opens too: on iPhone, iPad and Mac it shows as a chip, such as PDF document with its size, and a tap opens it. The inbox and alerts say Photo or Video, never the link. NIP-04 messages have no locked files and still send a plain link. You can select and copy text in a message on iPhone and Android. Links in a message can be tapped and open in the app's own browser ( more ). There is no way to delete a message. Did it go? Sending, Not sent, Try again A message says Sending… until a relay takes it. If none does, it says Not sent with Try again (on iPhone, iPad and Mac also Remove ). A message is never shown as sent when it wasn't, and never shows twice, even with a slow signer. (iPhone, iPad, Mac, Android and the web.) While your relays haven't answered, the inbox says Loading messages… instead of looking empty, and after about 10 seconds Your message relays aren't answering yet. Names load in the inbox and the conversation header, instead of a short key. On iPhone, iPad and Mac, what you typed stays as the conversation's draft when you leave it. Drafts are kept in memory only, so they don't survive a restart. A send that fails after you left puts the words back as the draft. Switching account closes the open conversation and drops its draft, so you never write as the wrong account. (iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android.) Reading older messages, a new one no longer pulls you down to the bottom. Encryption NIP-17 and NIP-04 Messages are sent with NIP-17 : the message is sealed and wrapped so relays can't see who it's from, who it's for, or what it says. A copy goes to you too, so your other devices see it. Some older apps only speak the older NIP-04 , which hides the text but not who's talking. Nostr Vault reads both. d: How Nostr Vault notifications work without APNs or FCM push on iPhone, Android, Mac and the web app: what wakes the app, when alerts arrive while it is open, in the background or closed, what to allow, and the limits.
h: Why there is no push · iPhone: when iOS lets it run · Android: your vault keeps running · Mac: always on while it's running · Web: only while a tab is open
x: Why there is no push Most apps get their alerts from a company server, which hands them to Apple (APNs) or Google (FCM) to send to your phone. That server sees who wrote to you and when. Nostr Vault has no such server. The relay inside the app collects what tags you, and the app makes the notification itself on your device. So an alert can only come while that relay is running. How often it can run is different on each device. On every device: Only people in your web of trust set off an alert. New followers from outside it are counted ("3 new followers") instead of named. If your web isn't built yet, strangers set off no alerts at all. With more than one account, each account's alerts follow its own web. A message alert says who it's from, not what it says, unless you turn on Show message text . The text never goes into a web alert. You choose the kinds under Settings → Notifications ( more ). Likes and reposts are off until you turn them on. While the app is open, new things show as a pill at the top, not as a system alert. With more than one account, each alert shows which account it's for, and each account's alerts are grouped together. In the account switcher, each other account shows how many new things it has. Something older than 24 hours never sets off an alert. When the vault catches up after being away, the first five items alert and the rest fold into one summary. iPhone and iPad iPhone: when iOS lets it run What wakes it: iOS's Background App Refresh. The app asks to be woken every 15 minutes at the earliest. iOS decides when that actually happens, based on how often you use the app, your battery and your connection. There is also a longer check that iOS only runs while the phone is charging and online. Open: things arrive right away and show as a pill at the top. They are also listed in Notification Center. In the background: the app keeps going for about 30 seconds after you leave it, then iOS pauses it. After that, alerts come only when iOS wakes the app. That can be minutes later or much longer. Swiped away: this stops your vault. iOS may not wake an app you swiped away until you open it again, so alerts wait until then. With a Mac: if your Mac is your vault, each wake asks it for what came in while the phone was asleep. The Mac is always listening, so less is missed. What to allow: notifications (the app asks during setup), and iOS Settings → General → Background App Refresh on for Nostr Vault. The app doesn't check that second one for you. Low Power Mode pauses Background App Refresh. The honest limit: an iPhone without a mobile or desktop vault is not instant. If you need alerts right away, keep a mobile or desktop vault running or open the app. Android Android: your vault keeps running What wakes it: nothing has to. Your vault runs as a service you can see: the Your Vault notification, which says Vault running and has a Stop Vault button. It listens to your relays all the time and checks for anything it missed every 15 minutes. Open: new things show as a pill. Pills you didn't look at are filed quietly under Missed while open . In the background or swiped away: alerts come right away, because the vault keeps running. After a restart or an app update: the vault starts again by itself, as long as Start Vault Automatically is on (it is unless you turned it off, under Settings → Your Vault ). Message alerts start again with it, without opening the app, unless you sign with Amber: Amber needs the app in front to open your inbox. Force stopped or Stop Vault: no alerts until you open the app again. Using another app's relay (such as Citrine) instead of the built-in one: Nostr Vault makes no alerts. What to allow: notifications. On Android 13 and newer, Android asks once, just after setup, and turning on Settings → Notifications asks again if you said no. h: What it is · One web per account · The globe · Trust paths and their web · My Web and rebuilding · What your web decides · Block, private block and nuclear unfollow · Who Can Reach You · On each device
x: What it is Nostr has no central moderator. Instead, Nostr Vault trusts who you trust. Your web has three rings: Following : the people you follow. Vouched : people that 10 or more of your follows follow. Further out : people your follows follow, but fewer than 10 of them. Your vault rebuilds the web on its own, once a day unless you change Refresh Trust List. If you follow very few people, it borrows from your follows' follows so a new account isn't empty. New in 3.2.2 One web per account With more than one account on a device, each one now has its own web, built from its own follows. Before 3.2.2 the app pooled every account's follows into one web, so someone followed by one of your follows and two of another account's follows counted as vouched for you. To you they were three hops out. The open account sees its own web in feeds, the Vault list, notifications and the WoT globe: you, your follows, and people enough of your own follows follow. Your other accounts get their alerts, their account badge and their Vault lines judged by their own web too. The vault's inbox lets someone in for an account only if they're in that account's own web (since 3.3.0). Each account also has its own Follow Distance and Minimum Followers: see Follow Distance . Until the open account's web has been built, and for a new account with fewer follows than Minimum Followers, the app shows the shared web instead. The WoT tab The globe Open the WoT tab. You're in the middle. Your follows sit on the first ring, Vouched people on the next, and everyone else is a faint outer shell. Each person always sits in the same spot, because their place comes from their key. Layers. The menu at the top left picks Everyone , Following or Vouched (the Hop 2 layer), each with a count, and Hop 3 , Hop 4 and Hop 5 ( the far rings ). Vouched shows up once your vault has counted your web. (All apps; the web app also keeps Further out .) Filters. Talk with you keeps people you've replied to, reposted, liked or zapped, or who did that to you. Follow you back keeps follows who follow you too. Find someone. Tap the magnifier and type a name. Your follows come first, then your web, then everyone else. Live stars. New posts from your web fly in as stars while you watch. Your follows and the rest of your web fly as plain stars; from further out, only zaps fly. Nobody you blocked or muted ever flies. My Web has three switches for it: Live stars , Friends of friends and Likes, reposts and zaps (on the Mac, the antenna menu in the WoT bar). (iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android.) The far rings: Hop 3, Hop 4 and Hop 5 Past your web are faint rings for the people three, four and five hops out. Your phone can't rank that many people itself, so a desktop Vault (a Mac or a Linux box) ranks them and sends the scores to your phone over the mesh. A Mac does this for itself. Picking a hop. Pick Hop 3 , Hop 4 or Hop 5 in the layer menu and the globe zooms out to that ring: your inner globe shrinks in place in the middle and the hop becomes its own spinning sphere around it, the same size as the Hop 2 globe. Drag and it turns with the inner globe. Its best-ranked people sit on the sphere's skin with their faces showing, all the way out to the edge. Tap one to open their card; the globe draws the path from them in through each layer to you. Each hop shows its best-ranked people, up to 300, labelled Found by your desktop Vault . h: Where to find it · Follow Distance · Fewer hops, less spam · Each account has its own · Hop 3, Hop 4, Hop 5 and the trust rank · The web app
x: What the app calls it Where to find it Setting Where What you pick Follow Distance Settings → Your Vault → Who Can Reach You , under Web of Trust . iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android. Only you , 1 hop or 2 hops (the default) Minimum Followers The same screen, just below. 0 to 100, default 3 Discovery Reach (the slider) Settings → Feed → Discovery Reach . iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android, once a desktop Vault has sent its scores. Everyone else is kept out." Who can reach you Follow Distance A hop is one follow away from you. Your follows are 1 hop out. The people they follow are 2 hops out. Follow Distance Who can reach your inbox and messages Only you Only you and your other accounts on this device. d: How Nostr Vault's mesh works: your phone or Mac serves your own photos over the mesh, with no public IP, domain or cloud. My Devices, Mobile vault mode, share pages and privacy.
h: What the mesh is · Your phone or Mac as your photo server · My Devices · Mobile vault mode · Share pages · Privacy · What works today
x: The basics What the mesh is Most phones and home computers can't be reached from the internet. They sit behind a home router, move between Wi-Fi and cell, and have no fixed address. That's why your photos normally live on someone else's server. The mesh (built on FIPS) is a network where you reach a device by its Nostr key (an npub) instead of an IP address. It works across home routers and mobile networks, and the connection between two devices is encrypted end to end. Nostr Vault uses it to let your devices reach each other, and to let other people fetch your photos from you. Photos stay trustworthy no matter who hands them over. On Nostr, a photo is named by its fingerprint (a hash). Whoever sends it, the app checks the fingerprint, and if it matches, it's the photo. If it doesn't, the photo is thrown away and loaded the normal way. Your own server Your phone or Mac as your photo server Your Nostr profile already keeps a list of where your media lives. You can add one more entry to that list: your mobile or desktop vault (a spare phone or your Mac), written as its mesh address. Add it under Settings → Media Servers → Your Vaults ; linking a device doesn't list it. Your everyday phone isn't listed. It goes after your normal media servers, so apps that don't know about the mesh carry on as before. An app that does know about it can ask your device for a photo directly, by its fingerprint, the same way it would ask any media server. Your photos still go to your normal servers too. Your device is one more place they can come from, and the one you own. On a Mac , the Nostr Vault app serves while it's open. Leave it running and your Mac is an always-on photo server. On a phone , it serves while the app is open, or full-time in Mobile vault mode on a spare phone. Step by step: your Mac as your photo server , mobile or desktop vault . It turns on when you connect your first device from Settings → Your Devices . You can also switch on Mesh yourself under Your Devices → Advanced → Mesh . Serving is off until it is on. Your devices, together My Devices My Devices is the list of your own phones, Macs, mobile vault and browser vault that reach each other over the mesh. Devices on this list sync with each other in full: your notes, your photos and your history. On one device open Settings → Your Devices and tap Connect a computer or phone (on the Mac, Connect a phone under Your Vault). That turns the mesh on. Or open Mesh settings (on iPhone and iPad, the Mesh button on the Profile tab), turn on Mesh and tap Link a device . One shows a code, the other scans it, then they swap. Both add each other. See Link a device . Something that can't scan, such as a Linux box, is added by its mesh address: tap Add a device , then paste the address under Paste instead . A device on the list shows a dot when it's in reach. You can link more than one Mac, and each new photo and file reaches all of your devices; phones keep a full copy by default. To check that everything arrived, tap Sync now on a vault's card in Settings → Your Devices . More on Your Devices and sync . An always-on vault Mobile vault mode Mobile vault mode turns a phone into a small always-on vault. Put an old phone on a charger at home, turn Mobile vault mode on under Share With Others , and it keeps serving. On iPhone it keeps the screen on, pauses when you leave the app and turns on again when you come back. On Android it keeps serving in the background while the vault runs. Your own devices in My Devices reach it in full. Everyone else can only read the photos in your posts, and only slowly: 1 MB/s shared between all of them, at most 256 MB each. On iPhone and Android they get 1 GB a day in total, then wait until the next day. They can read your public notes, as on any relay, but not your messages or private notes, and they can't change anything. Anyone not on the list can only read your public notes and the photos in them, and leave you a message if your inbox lets them. x: Your Devices is where your linked devices live: your Macs, a Linux box, your phones, iPads and a mobile vault. Each one gets a card. Every new photo and file you add reaches all of them over the mesh, and your notes and history sync between them. It replaces the old Desktop vault sync page. Open Your Devices iPhone, iPad and Android: Settings → Your Devices . Mac: Settings → Your Vault → Your Devices . Under Your devices there is a card for each device, with its role and whether it is in reach. Your vaults have Sync now (more on that below). Connect a computer or phone ( Connect a phone on the Mac) turns the mesh on if needed and starts the two scans on Link a device . Under Advanced are Mesh (rename or remove a device there) and Desktop Vaults : every Mac and Linux box that keeps your vault, reached over the mesh, by web address, or both, in the order your public lists use. See Desktop Vaults . More than one Mac Link as many Macs and Linux boxes as you like. Each one gets its own card and its own copy of everything your phone sends, and each is queued on its own, so one Mac being off doesn't hold up the others. There is no main one: each desktop Vault catches up on its own, and the order under Desktop Vaults sets which comes first in your public lists. Full copy, on by default On iPhone, iPad and Android, This phone has Keep a full copy on this phone . It is on for everyone, new and existing: every photo and file from your other devices shows up here, and each new file you add goes straight to every linked device over the mesh. Off: this phone keeps your notes, and fetches a file only when you open it. Wi-Fi only (under it): catching up on files waits for Wi-Fi. What you add on this phone still goes out right away. With Use this phone as an always-on vault on, full copy stays on. A mobile vault keeps everything. Files show up live When a photo or file lands on your mobile or desktop vault, the vault posts a small file note about it. Any device with its Media tab open hears that note and shows the new file at once, with no pull to refresh. Delete it everywhere and the tile goes away on the others too. Photos you save from the Media tab itself (the picker, Files, or a pasted link) go to your other devices the same way. The vault writes that note itself for anything it is given, so uploads from the web app, Android, older app versions or other Blossom apps show up too. The note is signed with the vault's own key, never your Nostr key. Sync now and waiting items Anything that can't reach a device yet waits on the phone for it. The vault card shows how many are waiting, or Nothing waiting . Tap Sync now to send straight away, and on your desktop vault to check that everything arrived: it ends with what was copied and how many are missing, or says why it stopped. The first time a new phone links to a desktop vault, it copies your full history from it on its own ( Copying your full history from the Mac… ; leave the app open). If the app closes, you see Copy was interrupted and it picks up the next time the vault starts. If some of the copy didn't save, it says so and tries again the next time the two devices meet. When a device is out of reach While a Mac, a Linux box or a linked phone is out of reach, the phone tries again at least every 2 minutes, and right away when the device comes back on the mesh. Nothing is dropped for being tried too often; only very old items give up. A mobile vault is different: while it is out of reach the phone tries after 1 minute, then waits twice as long each time, up to 6 hours, and gives up after 40 tries. Once the device answers but turns an item down, the phone backs off instead: 1 minute, then longer each time, up to 6 hours, for at most 40 tries. A Mac is in reach while Nostr Vault is open on it; a phone while the app is open or in Mobile vault mode. Your devices sign with mesh keys Each device has its own mesh key, made on that device. x: A desktop Vault is a Mac or a Linux box that keeps a copy of your vault and stays on. You can have as many as you like. Each one is reached over the mesh , by its web address , or both , and each gets its own sync and its own status. There is no "main" one any more. Desktop Vaults replaces the old one-address Desktop vault sync page. Open Desktop Vaults iPhone and iPad: Settings → Your Vault → Desktop Vaults , or Settings → Your Devices → Advanced → Desktop Vaults . Android: Desktop Vaults on your Vault page (it shows how many you have), or Settings → Your Devices → Advanced → Desktop Vaults . Mac: the Mac is a desktop Vault itself, so it has no list. Its own page is Settings → Public on the web ( below ). Linux box: also a desktop Vault itself. Its page has My Devices and Public on the web ( below ). Add a desktop Vault Tap Add a desktop Vault . A Vault needs at least one way in: Over the Mesh : Pair a new desktop over the Mesh starts the two scans ( Link a device ), or pick a desktop you already paired under Paired desktop . A desktop you pair joins your Vaults by itself. Web address : type its https:// address. Both. Then the mesh comes first and the web address is the fallback. An address or a desktop that is already one of your Vaults is refused, so each one is listed once. When a paired Mac tells your phone the web address it serves, and that matches a Vault you typed, the two become one Vault. What goes over which path Each Vault's row says how it's reached: Mesh only , Web only or Mesh and web , with its address. Mesh only Web only Mesh and web Public posts, reactions, lists, profile mesh web mesh first, web as fallback Photos and files in public posts mesh web either Direct messages and their files mesh web mesh first, web as fallback Drafts, private notes, chats, settings, accounts, private files mesh never mesh only A web-only Vault says so: "Holds your public posts, photos and messages. The mesh never uses your Nostr key. Your devices use their own mesh keys ( more ). Every Vault catches up on its own. When your phone hands a new post to a Vault to send for you, it picks the first Vault in your list that answers over the mesh. Several Vaults, and their order The list's order is the order your Vaults go into your public lists. On iPhone and iPad, drag a Vault to move it; on Android, use the up and down arrows. The first Vault comes first in your public lists, and other apps upload your media to the first media server. Moving a Vault republishes only the lists whose Vault entries change order. Turning a list switch on puts this Vault after your other Vaults and before your own entries. It never moves an entry that is already there. Two Vaults can both be public on the web. Nothing asks you to move it from one to the other, and nothing turns itself off. Other apps may only use the first few: about 4 relays and 3 DM inboxes. The Vaults stay in your order, so you choose which come first. Listed publicly Open a Vault to see its name, kind, How it's reached , its Last copy , and Listed publicly . h: What each kind does · 1. Turn on Mobile vault mode on the spare phone · 2. Add it to My Devices · Where new photos go
x: Your mobile or desktop vault is the vault that stays on. A desktop vault is a Mac or a Linux box. A mobile vault is a box or an old phone on a charger. Your other devices reach it over the mesh, so your notes and media have a home even when your phone is off. What each kind does Desktop vault · full history (a Mac or a Linux box): keeps all your history and syncs both ways with your phones. You can have as many as you like, reached over the mesh, by web address, or both. See Desktop Vaults and Your Devices and sync . Mobile vault · new posts (a spare phone or a box): keeps a copy of your new posts and media, and a full copy of every file (Mobile vault mode keeps Keep a full copy on this phone on). Your phone still sends your notes to your relays itself. This page shows how to set one up on a spare phone. 1. Turn on Mobile vault mode on the spare phone Install Nostr Vault on the spare phone and sign in with the same account. On iPhone, add your main phone under My Devices first (step 2). Mobile vault mode won't start with an empty list. Open Settings → Your Devices and, under This phone , switch on Use this phone as an always-on vault . It is the same switch as Mobile vault mode under Settings → Mesh → Share With Others . Leave it on a charger. On iPhone, Mobile vault mode keeps the screen on, pauses when you leave the app and turns on again when you come back. On Android it keeps serving in the background while your vault runs, and after a restart. Your devices in My Devices reach the mobile vault in full. Anyone else on the mesh can read your public notes and the photos in your posts, and slowly: 1 MB/s for all of them together, at most 256 MB each. They get 1 GB a day in total, then wait until the next day: Share With Others shows Sharing paused and when it starts again. Your own devices are never limited. They can't read your messages or private notes, or change anything. Share With Others on iPhone Share With Others on Android 2. Add it to My Devices The quickest way: on both phones tap Link a device and do the two scans (see Link a device ). Or add it by address, as below. On the spare phone, under This Device , copy its mesh address. On your main phone, open Settings → Mesh → Add a device . Under Paste instead , paste the address, tap Use , and pick Mobile vault · new posts . Add the main phone to the spare phone's My Devices too. From then on, your new notes and media also go to the mobile vault over the mesh, as a copy: your main phone still sends your notes to your relays itself, and keeps them too. Anything that can't reach the mobile vault waits on the main phone and goes when the app is open and the mobile vault is in reach: while it is out of reach the phone tries after 1 minute, then waits twice as long each time, up to 6 hours, and gives up after 40 tries. It also tries right away when the mobile vault comes back. Sync now on its card in Your Devices ( Send now under Mesh → Sync) sends it straight away. What's public. Linking a vault doesn't list it. If you add it under Settings → Media Servers → Your Vaults , its mesh address is listed in your media server list, in public, so other apps can fetch your photos from it. Strangers on the mesh can't fetch direct-message files from it. A desktop Vault's mesh address is listed only by its own Media over the Mesh switch (Beta, off by default). Media goes to the mobile vault signed with this phone's mesh key, so it goes without a tap even if your key is in a remote signer. Where new photos go New photos are saved on this device first. If you have a mobile vault, a copy goes to it over the mesh, and the mobile vault puts it on your public media server for you. If this device has its own media server, it uploads there itself.

x: A Linux box (see Get started on Linux ) joins your devices like a Mac does and is one of your Desktop Vaults . It has no camera, so the box shows a code and your phone scans it. Pair from the box's page The box keeps its own list of paired devices (Linux 3.3.0 and newer). On the box's page (Settings → This Box ), under My Devices , tap Add a device . If they match, tap They match on the phone, then tap They match: add this on the box, which also confirms what the phone will be. The box never accepts a device on its own. Your Nostr key is never used and nothing is published. The box keeps a copy of your vault from each device you pair. Remove next to a device takes it off at once: it can't copy from the box again, even after a restart. This is the only way to take a device off the box: your media server list no longer decides. The box's page Open the vault's address (for example http://raspberrypi.local:8080/ ), sign in as the owner, and go to Settings → This Box . Only the owner's account can read it. Status : how long it has run, its version, memory and disk. Storage : the vault folder, space used and free, and Move vault to… another folder or drive. The box stops serving while it copies. Mesh : whether the mesh is connected, how many peers, and the box's Mesh address . My Devices : the box's own address, each of your devices, Add a device and Remove ( above ). Public on the web : for a box with its own web address, Make this vault public on the web puts it in your relay list and DM inbox, after your other Vaults. Other boxes and Macs can be public too. A box with no web address is reached only by your own devices over the mesh. More on Public on the web . Update : Check for update and install . Updates are manual for now: install the newer package on the box. Keys: what the box holds The box never holds your secret key. It knows only your npub, which says whose vault it is. On its first start it makes its own mesh key, readable only by the mesh service. That key is how your devices recognise the box. Your own devices reach the whole vault. Anyone else on the mesh reaches only a small, rate-limited door. Nothing publishes your home IP address. d: Let Nostr Vault on your Mac serve your photos over the mesh, listed in your media servers, with no public IP, domain or port forwarding.
h: Turn it on · Who gets what · Privacy
x: Your Nostr profile keeps a list of where your media lives. Nostr Vault on your Mac can add itself to that list, written as its mesh address. Apps that can use the mesh then load your photos straight from your Mac. Apps that can't skip it and use your other media servers, as before. Turn it on On the Mac, open Settings → Your Vault → Mesh and switch on Mesh . The mesh engine runs inside the Mac app; there's nothing else to install. Add a phone under My Devices . The mesh starts once at least one of your devices is on that list, and the Mac then lists its mesh address in your media servers by itself. Keep Nostr Vault open. In Settings → Your Vault → Startup , turn on Launch at Login and Start Vault Automatically so it's always there. Share With Others on Mac: List in my media servers Who gets what Your own devices in My Devices reach the Mac's vault in full. Anyone else can only open photos and files by their link, at up to 1 MB/s. They can't read your notes or change anything. Your photos still go to your normal media servers too. The Mac is one more place they can come from, and the one you own. Privacy Your home IP isn't published. The list holds the Mac's mesh key, and the mesh finds it by key. Listing it does link your npub to the Mac's mesh key, in public. Removing it later doesn't erase older copies of your list that relays may still hold. List in my media servers (under Share With Others) and Address source (under Advanced) are only for an outside FIPS transport such as nostr-vpn. With My Nostr npub it lists your Nostr npub, not the Mac's mesh key. Leave them off otherwise. Has the Mac its own web address? Public on the web , also under Your Vault, lists it for everyone on the web, separate from the mesh. See Public on the web . More on how photos are checked on the way: The mesh .
