d: Take a device off My Devices so it can no longer reach your vault, and what to do when a phone with Nostr Vault is lost or stolen.
h: Remove a device · A lost or stolen phone
x: Removing a device from My Devices stops it reaching this device's vault. Do it on every device that has it on its list. Remove a device Open Settings → Your Devices → Mesh and tap the device under My Devices . On the Mac, use the remove button on its row. Tap Remove from My Devices and confirm (on Android, Remove ). With the Mac's minus button it goes at once. Repeat on each of your other devices. A device on Android, with Remove from My Devices What changes: It can no longer reach this device's vault, or learn its address. New notes and media stop going to it. If it's on your media server list, it stays there until you remove it under Settings → Media Servers → Your Vaults . Anything it already has stays on it. Removing a device doesn't wipe it. If it was a Mac and you have another one linked, the other Mac takes over its role. A lost or stolen phone Remove it from My Devices on your Mac, your mobile vault and your other phones, as above. Signer: if the phone signed through a signer app, revoke its connection in the signer. Your key was never on the phone. Local key: if your secret key was on the phone, it's locked with your key password. Someone with the phone still needs that password. If you think they have it, treat the key as exposed: a Nostr key can't be changed, so make a new account and tell people to follow it. Set up the new phone : sign in with your key or signer ( iPhone , Android ), then add it to My Devices on your other devices. Your notes come back from your relays, your Mac or your mobile vault. Your public posts are on public relays and stay there. A lost phone loses only what nothing else holds a copy of, which is why a mobile or desktop vault is worth having.

t: Mesh settings: finder relays and middle server
d: What the finder relays and the middle server do in Nostr Vault's mesh settings, what they can see, and when to change them.
h: Finder Relays · Middle Server
x: Open Settings → Your Devices → Mesh → Advanced . Most people never need to change these. On iPhone, changes apply the next time the mesh starts. On Android they apply right away. Mesh, Advanced Finder Relays Your devices post where they are on these relays, so your other devices can find them. Like any relay, they see this device's IP address. Swipe to remove one on iPhone, or tap Remove on Android. At least one must stay. Middle Server The middle server links two devices that can't reach each other directly. It's how this phone reaches anyone outside My Devices: the photos of people you follow, a browser vault, and visitors to your mobile vault. They never get this phone's address, but the middle server does see it. Which follows' photos your app loads is up to you; who can see your photos isn't a setting. Public (fips1, fips2.iris.to) : the default on iPhone and Android. None : only devices on the same network can connect. Follows' photos load from their web addresses instead, a browser vault only connects on the same network, and a mobile vault takes no visitors. Reset to defaults puts both lists back.

d: The Nostr Vault browser vault at nostrvault.app/relay/: a browser tab that keeps your notes and serves them to your own devices over the mesh. Pairing, signing once, Start mesh, the screensaver, My Devices, the web app's live Media and slow relays, and limits.
h: What the browser vault is · Pair your iPhone with the page · What it keeps and serves · The screensaver · When the tab closes · In My Devices · Live Media and slow relays in the web app · Limits and privacy
x: The basics What the browser vault is The browser vault keeps your notes like any vault, but it runs inside a web page, at nostrvault.app/relay/ . It stores notes in the browser's own storage on that device and joins the mesh, so your own devices can reach it by its key. New to the mesh? Read The mesh first. The page keeps no Nostr key of yours. You sign once to show which account is yours, and the key you sign with is not kept. Your notes arrive already signed, and the page checks each signature. A good spot for it is an old phone or tablet on a charger. Set it up Pair your iPhone with the page On your iPhone, open Mesh and turn the mesh on. Under This Device , tap Copy . That's the phone's mesh address. On the device that will run the page, open nostrvault.app/relay/ . Paste the address into the box under the Mesh heading (one address per line). Show the page which Nostr account is yours by signing once: tap Sign with extension , or paste an nsec, an ncryptsec (with its password below) or a bunker:// link and tap Sign with key . The key signs one proof and isn't saved anywhere. A typed npub is refused ("An npub can't sign."), because anyone can type an npub. Without a signed account the page turns your notes away and keeps 0. Forget account clears it. Tap Save owners . The page reloads. Tap Start mesh . The status's first line shows the page's own mesh address . There's no Copy button, so select the address and copy it. On the iPhone, go to My Devices → Add a device . Under Paste instead , paste the page's address, tap Use , and pick Browser vault . The phone then connects for the page. If it doesn't, open the page's entry in My Devices and tap Connect this phone . Copy this phone's mesh address is there too. A link of the form nostrvault.app/relay/#owner=npub1 also adds an owner. The npub in it is the phone's mesh address (from This Device ), not your Nostr account. The page asks you to confirm each address first, because an owner can write to the page and read everything on it. Only accept your own. What it does What it keeps and serves Your new notes. While the iPhone app is open, each new note you post also goes to the page. Send my latest notes sends your 20 most recent notes from the phone. The result line says how many the page kept. In this testing build, check that number: if it says 0 kept, the page did not take your notes. Checked notes only. The page checks each note's signature and turns away notes from authors it isn't set up for. Owners only, for notes. The page serves notes on the mesh only to the addresses saved as owners. Anyone else asking for notes is dropped without an answer. A public photo door. Like the apps, Start mesh also opens a public photo door on the mesh to anyone, and it answers only for photos that a public note names. Photos, read only. Under Show photo , you can paste a photo's fingerprint (sha256) or a .fips link and the page fetches it from a paired vault. It shows the photo only if the fingerprint matches. Photos aren't stored on the page. The page reaches your phone through the public mesh entry points (seeds). Once both ends are connected it tries a direct link. On the iPhone, leave the middle server under Advanced on its public setting. A browser vault has no same-network route, so with None it most likely can't reach your phone at all. Keep it awake The screensaver Start screensaver fills the screen with a black "relay running" view: a count, the uptime, whether the screen is kept awake (the wake lock), and whether the seed is up. Tap anywhere to leave it. After a reload it comes back on its own, and the wake lock is taken again when the tab is visible. The count on this screen is the page's own test notes, not your notes. Report shows storage, uptime gaps and a signature self-test, if you want the details. When it stops When the tab closes The relay only runs while the page is open and the screen is on. Closed, locked or in the background, nothing reaches it. Notes the phone sends w

d: What your vault keeps on each device: your notes, mentions, messages and media. Space for each account, who reads the private side, the Vault tab, Import Notes, and the Mac and web differences.
h: What your vault is · Every account on this device · The Vault tab · Vault settings · Import your past notes · Phone, Mac and web
x: The basics What your vault is Most Nostr apps only read and write to other people's relays. Nostr Vault also runs one on your device. Your vault is a Nostr relay and media server of your own, and it keeps a copy of: Your own notes , everything you post, like, zap and save. Notes that mention you , from people you trust (see Who Can Reach You ). Your direct messages , still encrypted. Recent notes from people you follow , so your feed loads fast. Older ones are cleared out over time. Your media , in its own media server. The notes and media of your other accounts on this device, each in its own space (see Every account on this device ). The vault's address ( wss://127.0.0.1: on a phone) only works on that device. Other apps and people can't connect to it directly. What reaches it over the mesh or the web is set out in Who Can Reach You . Your notes still go to your normal relays too. The vault is the copy you own. To see it explained in the app, open Settings → Help → Tutorials and play Your Vault at Work or How Your Vault Works . More than one account Every account on this device The first account you set up is the owner: the vault is theirs. Accounts you add in Settings → Accounts & Keys share the same vault, in two different ways. Space in the vault Reads the private side The owner Yes, always, even with only an npub Yes An account with a key or signer on this device Yes Yes A watch-only account (npub only) Yes on iPhone, iPad and Mac. No on Android No Space means the vault keeps that account's own notes and uploads, and shares them like yours. The private side is your private notes, your old list versions, the full list of your media, and media you never posted. Only the owner and accounts that can sign on this device read it, by signing in with their own key. A watch-only npub is often someone else's account. So it never reads the private side, and its notes can't be written into your private notes either. Only accounts that can read the private side can add to it. Removing an account's key or signer keeps its space but stops its private reads. Removing the account takes away both. After a copy from another device, iPhone, iPad and Mac ask Add your other accounts? The accounts you tick are added watch-only, each with its own space. iPhone and Android The Vault tab The Vault tab opens on Vault , a list of everything new. Tap the Vault button at the bottom right (or pick Vault Dashboard at the end of the mode menu) to see how your vault is doing. At the top it says Your vault is running , starting, paused or needs a restart, with how long it's been up. If it stops, a button lets you start it again so it catches up on new notes and messages. The menu on that card has Copy Address , Restart , Stop and Start . Below that: Is it safe? : where your key is (on this device, in a signer app, or none), then three checks: Follow list saved , List backups and Backup file , with a button to make a backup file. Who can reach you : how many people can send to your inbox, and how many people you've blocked. In your vault : how many events it holds and how much space notes, media and cache use. The cache is other people's media kept for quick loading, and you can clear it. A Good mornings line counts your own GM and Pura Vida notes, all time and today. It only counts short greetings (a GM with a photo counts, a long post that starts with GM doesn't), and it reads only your vault, so nothing is sent. Keep it full : Import notes , import media, back up media and export notes. Vault settings : shortcuts to Relays, Who Can Reach You, Media Servers, Desktop Vaults (with how many you have) and Start automatically. Then relay activity, and Advanced with Relay details . Mesh settings live in the Your devices card and media servers under Vault settings, once each, on every app (since 3.2.3). On iPhone and Android this screen is called Vault Dashboard . With more than one account on the device, chips over the Vault list switch between All and each ac

d: Nostr Vault's Who Can Reach You settings: Follow Distance, Minimum Followers and Refresh Trust List decide which people can send to your vault's inbox and messages. Spam control by Web of Trust.
h: What it controls · Follow Distance, Minimum Followers, Refresh Trust List · Who can see what · Phone, Mac and web
x: The basics What it controls Your vault has an inbox, where notes that mention you land, and a chat store for your direct messages. Anyone on Nostr can try to send to them. Who Can Reach You keeps out everyone who isn't close to you in your follows. This is your Web of Trust, and it's the vault's spam filter. Mentions and messages from people outside your trust list are turned away. Replies and quotes of your own posts still get in, from anyone. Your messages can only be read by people on the list who sign in. Your own notes aren't affected. You can always post. Open it from Settings → Your Vault → Who Can Reach You , or tap Who can reach you on the Vault Dashboard (Vault tab → Vault button), which shows how many people can reach your inbox right now. The settings Follow Distance, Minimum Followers, Refresh Trust List Follow Distance How far from you someone can be and still reach you. Lower is more private. A hop is one follow away from you, and you are never a hop, so the setting reads the same as a trust card. Follow Distance Who can reach you On a trust card Only you Only you and your other accounts on this device. 1 hop Also the people you follow. 1 hop 2 hops (default) Also the people they follow, if enough of your follows follow them (see Minimum Followers). 2 hops The control stops at 2 hops. An older, higher setting shows as 2 hops, which is how the relay always ran it. Nobody three hops out (a friend of a friend of a friend) gets into your inbox at any setting, unless they reply to or quote your own posts. The Vault Dashboard counts the same way: at the default its line reads "People within 2 hops of you", meaning your follows and their follows. A trust card calls that same friend of a friend "2 hops". Minimum Followers At 2 hops, how many of the people you follow must also follow someone before they can reach you. The default is 3: a friend of a friend gets in once 3 of your follows follow them. Raise it to keep out more strangers, lower it to let more friends of friends in. 0 and 1 both mean one follow is enough. It has no effect at Only you or 1 hop, and your own follows always count, whatever it's set to. A new account that follows fewer people than Minimum Followers would let almost nobody in, so the vault widens it to its follows' follows until the account follows more. With more than one account Since 3.3.0 each account has its own Follow Distance and Minimum Followers, and its inbox only lets in people from that account's own follows. Switch account to see or change its values. Your own accounts on the device can always reach each other. Refresh Trust List is one setting for the whole device. See Follow Distance . Refresh Trust List How often the vault rebuilds the list from your follows: Every hour , Every 12 hours , Every day (default) or Every week . Someone you just followed can reach you after the next rebuild. At a glance Who can see what There's no setting for who can see your vault. This is what each kind of visitor gets. Your devices Anyone on the mesh Anyone on the web Notes Yes No Yes, your public notes Private notes Yes No No, only you Photos Yes Only photos named in your public notes Yes, your public photos Messages Yes No Only people who sign in and are within your Follow Distance Your devices are the ones in My Devices . Your other accounts on this device have their own space in the vault, and only those that can sign here read private notes and messages: see Every account on this device . Where to find it Phone, Mac and web iPhone and Mac have the same screen. On the Mac it's in the Settings sidebar. Android has the same settings, and restarts the vault for you when you change one. The web has no Follow Distance. Its trust list is always 2 hops, as its Vault Dashboard says. Settings → Who Can Reach You has Minimum Followers and Refresh Trust List, kept in that browser. Its Who Can Reach You settings row opens the browser vault's mesh panel, where Who can reach this vault is a list of your own v

d: How to back up and restore Nostr Vault: export and import notes and media in Backup & Restore, restore an old follow list from Following Backup, un-delete posts in Recently Deleted, and the web backup.
h: Backup & Restore · Following Backup · List backups · Recently Deleted · Backups on the web
x: Notes and media Backup & Restore Open Settings → Backup & Restore (in the Your Vault group on iPhone, iPad and Android; on the Mac, Settings → Backups → Backup & Restore ). It has two parts, and each one is its own file. Notes. Export Notes (on the Mac, Save JSONL Backup ) saves everything in your vault as a .zip: your notes, private notes, messages (still encrypted), the notes that mention you and your feed cache. Import Notes puts a notes backup back. Media. On iPhone, iPad and Mac, save your photos and videos with Back up media on the Vault dashboard, under Keep it full ; Import Media here puts a media backup back. On Android this page has both Export Media and Import Media . On iPhone the file goes to the share sheet, so you can save it to Files or send it to your Mac. On the Mac and Android you pick where to save it. A restore adds to what's already in the vault. Anything it already has is skipped, and nothing is deleted. The vault pauses for a moment while notes are saved or restored. If any note or file fails to restore, it says so instead of reporting success, and a file that isn't a media backup is turned down. Your keys are not in the backup. A backup holds notes and media only. Keep your key (or your signer) safe on its own; see Accounts & Keys in the app. Your wallet connection and signer links aren't in your phone's own device backup either: they stay in the phone's secure storage, on that phone only. On iPhone, iPad and Mac your message cache is left out of the device backup too. On a new phone, connect your wallet and signer again. Start the vault before you back up media. The Vault dashboard has both under Keep it full : Export notes and Back up media . Your follow list Following Backup A follow list on Nostr is one list that gets replaced every time it changes. A buggy app can wipe it. Nostr Vault keeps a snapshot each time your list changes, up to 50, on your device. Open Settings → Following Backup . Pick a snapshot. It shows who you no longer follow and who was added since. You can re-follow one person, or tap Restore This List to put the whole list back. Confirm. The restored list replaces your current one and is published to your relays. If your list was wiped somewhere else, Scan Relays looks for older copies of it on your relays. Every list you keep List backups Your vault also keeps the old versions of your other lists: mutes, bookmarks, relays, follow sets and more. Open List backups from the Vault dashboard or Settings (on the web, Recover a List ). Each version says which app saved it and what changed. If a list suddenly shrinks, a banner warns you, and Merge puts the old entries back alongside the new ones, so nothing you added since is lost. Look up and back up my lists (on by default, on the Vault dashboard; on Android also while you set up) goes further back: it asks history relays for older copies of your lists, the way the Lazarus spec finds them, and saves them in your list history. A follow list another app emptied months ago can still come back. It runs from the Vault's Still to bring in card, as Old versions of your lists . Undo a delete Recently Deleted Posts you delete on a device stay in Settings → Recently Deleted on that device for 30 days. Un-delete posts it again as a new post. Likes and replies on the old post don't come back. Delete Forever removes the copy now. Profiles, lists and articles aren't kept here. Recently Deleted is in the apps and the web app. In the browser Backups on the web The web app keeps its vault in your browser, so back it up if it holds anything you don't have elsewhere. Settings → Backup & Restore : Export notes saves your notes, private notes, messages, the notes that mention you and feed cache as the same .zip the phone apps make, so either one restores the other. Then tap Save backup file to keep it. Photos and videos aren't in it. Vault Dashboard → Keep it full → Back up media saves this browser's photos and videos as a .zip. The web app can't import me

d: Media servers (Blossom) in Nostr Vault: where photos go when you post, Upload Quality (Standard or Original), adding and removing servers, Auto-Mirror and Import media, the live Media tab across your devices, cache settings, and uploading from the share sheet.
h: What a media server is · Where a photo goes when you post · Upload Quality · Add or remove a media server · Mirroring · Deleting a photo · Media & Cache · htree photos · Leftover files clear themselves · The Media tab · Uploading from the share sheet · Import media · Picture in picture · Your device as a photo server
x: The basics What a media server is Relays only carry text. A photo or video is too big for that, so it goes to a media server instead, and your note holds a link to it. Nostr media servers speak a shared language called Blossom , so any Nostr app can read from them. A photo on a Blossom server is named by its fingerprint (a hash of the file). The same photo has the same name on every server, so it can be copied between servers and still be checked. Your account publishes a list of your media servers. Other apps read that list to find your files. When you post Where a photo goes when you post The app first saves the photo on this device, in your vault. It then uploads it to all of your outside media servers at once. As soon as one of them has it, the note is sent. The other servers keep uploading in the background. If no outside server takes the photo, the post is not lost. It waits under Settings → Media Servers in Waiting to send , and sends itself when a server answers. Tap Try sending now to retry straight away, or tap the bin next to a post to drop it. Posting a photo still needs a public media server. A photo that is only on your phone can't be seen by anyone else, so the app won't post it without an outside server. Smaller uploads Upload Quality Since 3.3.0 the app shrinks photos and videos before it uploads them, so posts go up faster, load faster for everyone, and fit on more media servers. One setting decides it: Upload Quality , with two choices. Standard (the default): a photo's long edge is brought down to at most 2048 pixels and it is saved as a JPEG, which also drops everything the camera wrote into it (model, serial number, date, location). On iPhone, iPad, Mac and Android a video is made 720p (1280 720, or 720 1280 upright) at up to 5 Mbps. Files that are already small go up as they are, a screenshot or other PNG stays a PNG, and GIFs and other moving pictures are never changed. Original : photos and videos go up as they are. The files are bigger, and some media servers refuse large ones. The location is removed either way. Original is never a way to post where a photo was taken. It covers the photos and videos you post in a note, share to Nostr Vault from another app, send in live chat or send in a message. There is no switch on each photo: change the setting before you post. Profile pictures, banners, article covers and listing photos keep their own sizes whatever you pick. The Media tab always keeps the original. Files you add on the Media tab (Vault → Media on the web) are your own copies, so they are never shrunk. Where to find it: iPhone, iPad and Mac: Settings → Media Servers , in the Upload Quality section. Android: Settings → Media & Cache → Upload Quality . The web app and Nostr Vault for Linux (whose window is the web app): Settings → Media & Cache , under Uploads. The web app shrinks photos only: videos go up as they are, because a browser can't re-encode them. A HEIC photo that the browser can't open (Chrome and Firefox) also goes up as it is. The choice is kept in this browser. Your list Add or remove a media server Open Settings → Media Servers . It sits in the Relays group, under Relays. Add: type the server's address (for example blossom.example.com ) in the box and tap the add button next to it. If you leave out https:// , the app adds it. Remove: tap the red button next to a server (a minus sign on iPhone and Mac, a bin on Android). Under Suggested , tap Add next to a well-known server to add it. Prices and limits are set by each server. Each change is saved and your updated list is published to your relays. Every desktop Vault with a web address is used as a media server too: uploads also go to it. On iPhone, iPad and Android it shows at the top under Added for You , and you don't add it by hand. Whether other apps see it is that Vault's own Media servers switch, so its entry shows under From your desktop Vaults , read only here. A desktop Vault's mesh address is listed only by its own Media

d: How Nostr Vault share links work: Share and Copy Link make a nostrvault.app/thread/ link that opens the post in any browser as a guest, with a link preview card. Plus sharing photos into the app.
h: Share or copy a link · The link preview · Opening a link, with or without an account · Sharing photos into Nostr Vault
x: Sharing a post Share or copy a link Open the menu on any post. Share opens your phone's or browser's share sheet, so you can send the link in a message, an email or another app. Where a browser has no share sheet, it copies the link. On Android it's titled Share Note . Copy Link (Android and web: Copy link ) puts the link on your clipboard and shows Link copied . The link looks like https://nostrvault.app/thread/nevent1 . The nevent part names the post and its author, so the link works without any account and doesn't depend on one relay. Articles, videos and other posts have a Share button too, and give the same kind of link. A live stream's link ends in naddr1 instead. Its menu also has Share as a note , which starts a note saying "Live now: host " with the stream's live card. In a chat or a feed The link preview When you paste the link in a chat app or a social site, it shows a preview card: the author's name (" on Nostr"), the start of the post, and the photo if the post has one. What they see Opening a link, with or without an account The link opens the post in the Nostr Vault web app, in any normal browser. No account? They read the post and its replies as a guest. A bar at the bottom says Viewing as a guest , with Get the app and Sign in . They can open profiles and come back to the post. Hashtags and messages ask them to sign in. Want to reply or like? Liking, replying, reposting and zapping need them to sign in. After signing in, the web app opens on the same post. Already signed in to the web app in that browser? The post opens in their account. A guest visit keeps nothing. Nothing is signed, and nothing is saved in the browser once the tab is closed. Photos load from their usual media server. If one can't be loaded there, the browser fetches it from the author's own device over the mesh. See The mesh . Deleted posts. If the author deletes the post, the link says This post was deleted by its author. Anyone who already saw it may still have a copy, as with anything you post publicly on Nostr. The other direction Sharing photos into Nostr Vault You can also send photos and videos from your Photos app or gallery to Nostr Vault, to upload them to your media server (Blossom). iPhone: pick up to 20 photos and 20 videos, tap Share, choose Nostr Vault, then Add to the upload queue . Open Nostr Vault, or tap the Ready to upload to your media servers notification, to finish the upload. Android: share one or more photos or videos to Nostr Vault. The upload starts right away and shows Uploading to your media servers . Set up your account first. Uploading needs a public media server; see Settings → Media Servers .

d: Share profile in Nostr Vault: a QR code and a nostrvault.app/p/ link for any profile, Copy link and Share, and what happens when someone scans or opens the link.
h: Open the share sheet · Opening a profile link · Who told you about Nostr Vault? · On each device
x: Share profile Open the share sheet Your own profile: tap the QR code button (Android: the share button) next to Edit Profile . Anyone else's profile: open the menu and tap Share profile . The sheet shows a large QR code with the person's name and picture, and three ways to pass it on: Show the code. Someone points a phone camera, or the scanner in Nostr Vault, at it. Copy link puts the link on your clipboard and says Copied . Share opens the system share sheet, so you can send the link in a message, an email or another app. The link looks like https://nostrvault.app/p/npub1 . It carries only the public key, never a secret key. The other side Opening a profile link Scanned or pasted in Nostr Vault. The code from the setup scanner, or a link pasted into Search , opens the profile straight away. Search also takes a bare npub, an nprofile or a nostr: link. Opened in a browser (a tapped link, or a code scanned with the phone camera). The page shows the profile's name, picture and bio, with Open in Nostr Vault to jump into the app, Get Nostr Vault if they don't have it, and Open in another Nostr app . New to Nostr Vault? If they open the link and then install and set up the app, the person who shared it is already filled in on the Who told you about Nostr Vault? step. See below . During setup Who told you about Nostr Vault? A new account starts with an empty feed. One setup step fixes that with the person who brought you here. Tap Scan their profile code , or paste their profile link or npub and continue. Tap Skip, nobody told me to leave the step out. Their profile card shows, so you can check it's them. Tap Follow with their name, or Not them? Try another . Next come the people they follow and who follow them, the ones they talk with most first. Nobody is picked for you: tap someone to see their profile, and tap Follow there. Tap the button that says how many you'll follow. You follow them and everyone you picked, as one follow list, once setup finishes. When you create an account, the step comes after your profile and the servers step on iPhone, and straight after your profile on Android. When you bring an account you can post with, it comes after the relay check (Android: right after you enter your key). On Android the buttons read Skip and Not them? Change. Read-only accounts skip it. Details for each device: iPhone , Android , Mac . On each device iPhone, iPad and Android have everything on this page. A profile link opened before setup fills in the Who told you step. Mac has Share profile, and a link pasted into Search opens the profile. Links don't open the Mac app from a browser, so paste the link into the Who told you step yourself. Web has Share profile (QR code, Copy link, Share) on every profile.

d: Fixes for common Nostr Vault problems: empty feed, signer not answering, read-only account, photo posts failing, relays not answering, mesh devices not in reach, Check sync stopping, Mobile vault mode paused.
h: My feed is empty · Underrated is empty · I can't post, like or follow · My signer never answers · My photo post didn't send · A relay isn't answering · Android: my vault went quiet after an update · A device on My Devices is never in reach · Check sync stops early · Someone's photos don't load over the mesh · Mobile vault mode paused · Message alerts don't show what was said · A link opens inside the app, not in my browser · Still stuck?
x: My feed is empty You see "No Following Feed". Nostr has no algorithm, so a new account starts with nothing: you see posts from people you follow. Fix: follow a few people. Fill Your Feed helps you find them by topic, and five follows builds your web of trust, which fills Discover and Global too. Replay it from Settings → Help → Tutorials . More on Feeds . Global and Media also stay empty until your web is built. That's on purpose: they show nothing rather than everyone. Underrated is empty You see "Underrated needs your wider web". Underrated picks posts from people one step out, so it needs your wider network: the people your follows follow. Fix: tap Build your wider network and give it a few minutes. New accounts build it by themselves after setup; an account set up before 3.2.2 may need the tap once. I can't post, like or follow You see "Read-only for now", "No private key stored for this account" or "This account is read-only. Add its key to follow." You signed in with an npub or a name@domain, which lets you look but not sign. Fix: add the account's key or connect a signer in Settings → Accounts & Keys . My signer never answers You see "Your signer didn't answer in time", "Clave didn't answer" or, on Android, "Amber signing was cancelled or timed out". Your signer app has a request waiting that you haven't approved, or it can't reach its relay. Fix: open the signer app, approve the pending request, then tap Retry in Nostr Vault. If it says "Couldn't reach your signer's relay", check your connection. "This signer is for a different account" means the signer holds another key than the account you picked. My photo post didn't send You see "Your post wasn't sent: no outside media server is set up". A photo has to sit on a public media server so other people can see it, even with the mesh. Fix: add a server in Settings → Relays → Media Servers , then post again. If it says your Mac didn't take the photo, check that Nostr Vault is open on your Mac. "Saved on this device" means the post will send itself as soon as the server answers. A relay isn't answering In the relay list you see " relay isn't answering". It didn't answer just now. Relays go down. Fix: leave it a while. If it stays down, remove it, then tap Save : nothing in the relay list changes until you save. "No Write relay" means none of your relays is set to Write. Your posts still go out, to the default relays the message names, but mark at least one of yours as Write so they go where you choose. Android: my vault went quiet after an update Installing an update stops the app, and with it your vault. Fix: open the app once after updating. Keep Start Vault Automatically on: newer builds then start the relay again by themselves after an update. A device on My Devices is never in reach Under Mesh settings → My Devices a device stays "Not in reach" (Android shows when it was last seen). A mobile or desktop vault only answers devices that are on its own My Devices list, and a Mac with an empty list doesn't start the mesh at all. Fix: link the two again with Link a device : two scans, and both devices add each other. Check that Mesh is on, on both, and that Nostr Vault is open on the Mac. See Link a device . Check sync stops early On iPhone and Android, Sync now on your Mac's card in Settings → Your Devices (it used to be called Check desktop vault sync) ends on "Stopped · N still missing", "Copy didn't finish" with a reason, or "Copy was interrupted". The button is greyed out while a copy is running or when your vault isn't running. Fix: read the reason line. "Copy was interrupted" means the app closed during the copy; it picks up again the next time the relay starts. Anything that couldn't be copied is tried again once a day, and tapping the button starts a new run. Someone's photos don't load over the mesh Your app only asks the mesh for photos from people you follow, and only if they list their own vault as a media server. Files over 32 MB always come from the normal web

d: Nostr Vault FAQ: which version is current, is there a Linux version, can I use my existing Nostr account, which relays my posts go to, do I need a Mac, is my home IP public, who can see my photos, losing a phone, what the web app does, is it free.
h: Which version is current? · Is there a Linux version? · Is it free? Is it open source? · What is the vault? · Can I use my existing Nostr account? · Which relays do my posts go to? · Do I need a Mac? · Why does posting a photo still need a server? · Is my home IP public? · Who can see my photos over the mesh? · What if I lose my phone? · Why do links open inside the app? · Why don't message alerts show the text? · What can the web app do?
x: Which version is current? 3.3.0, on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Android, the web and Linux. The Android and Linux builds are on GitHub ; the App Store and Zapstore show the version they have on their own pages. 3.0 added the mesh, which connects your own devices directly; 3.1.0 added a new composer and your own choice of relays; 3.2.0 links your devices with two scans and copies your whole vault to a new one; 3.2.2 opens links inside the app, adds Your Devices in Settings and keeps your drafts encrypted; 3.2.3 adds private blocks, nuclear unfollow, one web-of-trust gate on every feed, light mode and Nostr Vault for Linux in beta; 3.3.0 adds Desktop Vaults, a trust rank out to six hops and the first stable Linux release. See What's new . Is there a Linux version? Yes, stable since 3.3.0 (in beta from 3.2.3). It turns a Raspberry Pi, a mini PC, a home server or a desktop into your always-on vault, with a window and tray icon on a desktop. There are packages for Debian, Ubuntu and Raspberry Pi OS (.deb), Fedora (.rpm), Arch and Alpine, a Flatpak for desktops, and a Nix flake with a NixOS module, for arm64 and amd64. See Get started on Linux . Is it free? Is it open source? Yes to both. The app is free and the code is MIT licensed, on GitHub . What is the vault? Your vault is a personal Nostr relay and a media server, running on your phone. It keeps your notes, your messages and your photos on the device. Nobody on the network can connect to it, unless you share it with your own devices over the mesh. Can I use my existing Nostr account? Yes. Tap Bring an account instead of Create an account (on the web, No, I already use Nostr ). iPhone and Mac: paste your nsec, an encrypted key (ncryptsec) or a bunker link, or Use a signer app and Sign in with Clave . Android: paste a key or bunker link, Use Amber , or Use a signer app . Web: Sign in with extension or Connect bunker . The web app never takes the nsec of an account you already have. An npub or name@domain also works, read-only: you can look around but not post. Which relays do my posts go to? The Write relays in Settings → Relays , and only those. If your account already has a relay list, the app uses it. A new account chooses its own when it's set up: we suggest some, and you can take them, remove any or add your own. If your list has no Write relay, posts still go out, to the suggested relays the warning names. Your own vault always keeps a copy. Edits to your relays are kept only when you tap Save (on the web, Save and publish ), which also publishes your relay list for other apps. Do I need a Mac? No. Your phone runs its own vault. A Mac or a Linux box is an optional extra: as Desktop vault · full history it can hold a full copy and serve your photos while it's on. You can have several: see Desktop Vaults . A spare phone in Mobile vault mode can do the same job. Why does posting a photo still need a server? Other people need to be able to see it, from any app, whether or not your phone is on. So a photo you post also goes to a public media server. The mesh is an extra, faster place to fetch it from, not a replacement. If posting fails . Is my home IP public? No. Once you add a device, only your own devices learn your phone's address. Anyone else gets your public photos and never your address, but the mesh's middle server does see it. You can change or turn off the middle server under the mesh's Advanced settings. Who can see my photos over the mesh? Your own devices get everything. Anyone else gets only photos that are in your posts, and only within limits: 1 MB/s in total, 1 GB a day on an iPhone (1 GB per sharing session on other devices) and 256 MB per file. Nobody else can read your notes. Your posted photos are on public media servers too, so treat them as public. What if I lose my phone? On each of your other devices, open the lost phone under My Devices and tap Remove from My Devices . The mesh restarts and the lost phone is cut off at once. The phone's mesh address is its own

d: How another Nostr client can read photos over the FIPS mesh: the fipsmesh:// address form in kind 10063, plain Blossom GETs, and the NIP-F1 draft.
h: Other NIPs worth knowing · Build Nostr Vault
x: The mesh address is one new entry form, fipsmesh://<npub>/ , in lists you already use: the media server list ( kind:10063 ) and, later, the relay list ( kind:10002 ). In a relay list it goes in its own fipsmesh tag, not an r entry, so clients without mesh support never try to connect to it; Nostr Vault doesn't publish that tag yet. Linking a device never writes the media server list: Nostr Vault adds a fipsmesh entry only when you turn on a desktop Vault's Media over the Mesh switch (Beta, off by default; on a Mac, under Public on the web), or add a vault yourself under Media Servers → Your Vaults on the Mesh and save. Mesh entries always go after the https servers, and a list of mesh entries only is refused. No new event kinds. Requests are plain Blossom GET /<sha256> , with the same hash check. A client that doesn't know the form skips it and carries on with the other servers in the list. A client that does can ask the device for the photo by its fingerprint, the same way it asks any media server, and throws the photo away if the fingerprint doesn't match. Draft, not yet submitted NIP-F1: Nostr over the FIPS Mesh The address form, transport, safety rules for serving and reading, and where Nostr Vault implements each part. Read the draft → How it works for people using the app is on The mesh . Other NIPs worth knowing NIP-F1 in Nostr Vault is Beta. The app's What is this? (NIP-F1) link lands here. Mesh entries in your public lists are optional: every list still works for clients that skip them. Nostr Vault publishes the media entry ( kind:10063 ) only from the Media over the Mesh switch, off by default. The relay entry ( kind:10002 fipsmesh tag) is planned and not published yet. Details: NIP-F1-IMPLEMENTATION.md . Drafts (NIP-37). Drafts are kind:31234 with only d and k tags outside; the draft itself is NIP-44 encrypted to your own key. Older plaintext drafts are re-saved encrypted once. They go to your own vault, not to public relays. File notes (NIP-94). Your vault keeps a kind:1063 note for each file in your media, on its own /files relay. Only you and the readers you name can read it. Encrypted files in messages (NIP-17 kind:15 ). Test vectors are in docs/DM_FILE_VECTORS.json . The file is encrypted before upload and goes to your first media server over HTTPS, like the message. Build Nostr Vault Everything is in one repository, btcforplebs/nostr-vault : HavenApp/ : the iPhone, iPad and Mac app (Swift). just ios-build or just macos-build . NostrVault/ : the Android app (Kotlin). just android-build . haven-go/ : the relay (Go), compiled into the apps as libhaven . web-vault/ : the web app. npm ci , then npm run dev or npm run build . web-relay/ : the browser vault . fips-bridge/ , fips-v2/ and fips-v2-android/ : the mesh (FIPS) engine embedded in the apps, and its probes (Rust). linux/ : Nostr Vault for Linux. linux/native/build.sh arm64 amd64 builds the .deb, .rpm and Arch packages on Debian 12, packaging/alpine/ the Alpine apk and linux/flatpak/ the Flatpak. Installing the newer package is the update. See Get started on Linux . docs/ : the NIP drafts, including NIP-F1, and the contracts between the apps and the vault.
